requirement: Run named async health checks concurrently, cancel the rest on the first expected failure, and raise that failure plainly instead of as an ExceptionGroup.
skeleton: A CheckFailedError with name and cause, a _guard wrapper, and run_checks using asyncio.timeout around a TaskGroup and unwrapping its ExceptionGroup.
caption: A health-check runner using asyncio TaskGroup and asyncio.timeout with collections.abc and typing. Each check is wrapped so an OSError or ValueError becomes CheckFailedError carrying the check name and cause; the TaskGroup cancels the siblings, and run_checks unwraps an ExceptionGroup made only of CheckFailedError into the one with the smallest name, raised from None. Other exceptions keep their ExceptionGroup, the deadline raises TimeoutError, and an empty mapping or non-positive deadline raises ValueError. The fixture asserts ordered results, sibling cancellation, the bare first failure, group preservation, the deadline and the ValueError cases.

constraints: A failure cancels every sibling check
Only an all-CheckFailedError group is unwrapped
Simultaneous failures pick the smallest name
The unwrapped error is raised from None
An empty mapping or non-positive deadline raises ValueError

rationale.teaches: Let TaskGroup handle cancellation, then use ExceptionGroup.subgroup to unwrap only the expected failure type deterministically.
rationale.why: Callers that expect one error get an ExceptionGroup, or a nondeterministic error when several checks fail together.

ops.docstring: Run health checks in a TaskGroup and surface the first failure plainly.

ops.stmt: from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Mapping

candidates.why_wrong: The raised error keeps its original cause chain instead of from None.
The largest name is chosen when several checks fail together.
ValueError from a check is not wrapped as CheckFailedError.
A deadline of zero is accepted instead of raising ValueError.
The deadline is validated but never enforced on the checks.
